brief: JPM's Tactically Bullish call survives October's AI-driven selloff (NDX down 4.8% over two trading days, SPX -56bp last week). The desk expects a Tech rebound because NDX historically rebounds about 3% the week after a greater-than-3.5% Friday decline within 6% of highs, and recommends a Tech/Cyclicals barbell weighted toward Cyclicals. Three supports are cited for staying bullish rather than fearing recession: resilient household net worth, cash levels and corporate margins argue against mass layoffs even if AI capex slows (CRWV itself employs only 550 people); oil markets have already priced a Middle East re-escalation, which JPM says limits further downside to equities and upside to yields; and November and post-midterm seasonality are historically strong. Separately, midterms are forecast a 66%-probability Blue Wave, which gridlock should keep from producing real AI regulation, and SPX has risen every year after every midterm since 1950. Hedge funds had a brutal October (global long-short spread -2.2% MTD) despite flat indices, driven by AI-linked de-grossing; prior similarly sharp drawdowns rebounded in 6 of 7 cases. Jason Hunter flags S&P technical support at 7616-7643, below which selling could extend toward the 7200s.
